outcome_variable_scope: Agreement with REAL HUMAN pairwise rankings and own-minus-donor attribution, satisfaction from r04's tensor, donor under seed 20260727. Only the RESAMPLING UNIT varies.
scope: This is about intervals, not estimates: no point estimate in this package changes. It also does not license replacing published prompt-bootstrap intervals wholesale. The two-way crossed half-width IS estimated here, but by applying the CGM decomposition to bootstrap percentile half-widths as sd proxies -- an approximation valid for near-symmetric draws, which is why the three one-way inputs are stored alongside it.
verdict: P PROMPT-DOMINATED. The reframed object is M(R,J,pi,Q,P) with each layer validated separately, and P is the human population -- yet every interval in this package resamples PROMPTS. Measured before writing the round: 1011 annotators over 968 prompts, median 16 prompts each, only 1.5% rating a single prompt, and the top 10% of annotators holding just 12.7% of the links. The design is CROSSED and crossed almost uniformly, so prompt resampling accounts for prompt sampling and NOTHING for annotator sampling. Identical counts, three resampling units: by prompt, attribution half-width 0.0123 and agreement 0.0093; by ANNOTATOR, 0.0055 and 0.0056; by individual PAIR, 0.0049 and 0.0040. The annotator-clustered interval is 0.45x the prompt-clustered one on attribution and 0.60x on agreement, against a threshold of 1.25x fixed before the run. THE POINT ESTIMATES DO NOT MOVE -- agreement 0.6860, attribution +0.1215 under all three, because all three resample the same precomputed counts; a point shift would have been a bug, not a finding. DEGENERATE CONTROL: the pair-level design ignores both clusterings and is the NARROWEST of the three, as it must be -- the round refuses to run otherwise, because a bootstrap that cannot order its own designs cannot be used to compare two of them. THE CONFOUND, WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN: annotators are not randomly assigned to prompts, and this release is ordered by collection form, so an annotator-clustered interval could absorb prompt composition. Measured: 931 of 1011 annotators (92.1%) contribute to BOTH forms, and the near-uniform crossing with no whales is evidence against a few annotators driving the width. It does not eliminate the confound; it bounds how much room it has. WHY NARROWER, MECHANISM NOT MYSTERY: an annotator draw still touches 100% of prompts, because each annotator spans ~16 of them, so between-prompt variance is averaged out WITHIN each draw; a prompt draw touches only 63% and exposes it fully. The dominant variance component here is BETWEEN PROMPTS, not between people. THE ACTUAL ANSWER IS THE TWO-WAY INTERVAL, and it is computed rather than conceded: Cameron-Gelbach-Miller gives a crossed half-width of 0.0125 on attribution against the prompt-only 0.0123, i.e. the published interval understates by 2%; on agreement 0.0101 against 0.0093, 8%. That is an APPROXIMATION -- it applies the CGM decomposition to percentile half-widths as though they were sds, which holds only for near-symmetric draws -- so the three inputs are stored for recomputation. SCOPE: this changes no point estimate anywhere in the package. It changes what the intervals beside them mean, and the change is small.
